Actually the Oregon Public Retirement System Employee contributions before 1996 (Tier 1 Employees) contributed 6% of their income which was matched by the State of Oregon for a total of 12%. They were also guaranteed a Return on their pension fund of 8%. If the investment funds made more that 8% the pension fund got to keep the money. If the public employment retirement fund did not make 8% then the Tax payers of the state of Oregon had to make up the Difference. In 1996 that was changed (Creating Tier 2 employees) and the Employee contributions are capped at 6% with Matching contribution from the state of Oregon. Tier 2 employees have individual accounts which are easier to administer if they change jobs as they move back and forth between the public sector and private sector. The individual account is also now capped at 8% or market rate of return which ever is less.. Retired Oregon Public Employees now can retire at the age of 60 or after 30 years of accredited service. Their retirement benefit is calculated based on their final monthly salary multiplied by (since 1993, 1.5% for regular employees and 1.8% for Police and Fire.) State and local Office holders get 1.35% of their final monthly salary. All retiree's get a annual 2% Cost of Living Adjustment.

Of course the fly in the ointment is that if a Public Employee doesn't take any vacations, for their last two or three years, or use his/her sick days, (and most do) they get paid for unused vacations and sick days. The result is his or her final monthly salary may be 400 to 500% higher than the real salary. So if you make $ 51,000 year you have a monthly salary of $4250 a month.
